set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Gram-positive cells are described as physically strong. How are Gram-negative cells described?
opts: Physically strong
Physical strength is the Gram-positive description, from the thick peptidoglycan; Gram-negative cells are chemically strong.
Heat resistant
Heat resistance is not the contrast drawn; the pairing is physically strong Gram-positives against chemically strong Gram-negatives.
Spore protected
Neither group of medically important cocci forms spores; Gram-negative cells are described as chemically strong.
Chemically strong
Correct: Gram-positive cells are physically strong from thick peptidoglycan, whereas Gram-negative cells are chemically strong.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which enzyme, produced by 97% of human isolates, is a significant diagnostic trait of Staphylococcus aureus?
opts: Coagulase
Correct: coagulase coagulates plasma and blood, and its presence is what separates Staphylococcus aureus from the coagulase-negative staphylococci.
Staphylokinase
Staphylokinase does the opposite job, digesting blood clots; it is a virulence enzyme rather than the diagnostic trait.
Hyaluronidase
Hyaluronidase digests connective tissue; it is a virulence enzyme rather than the significant diagnostic trait.
Lipase
Lipases digest oils and other lipids and enhance colonization of the skin; coagulase is the diagnostic trait.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which Staphylococcus aureus toxin lyses neutrophils and macrophages?
opts: Coagulase
Coagulase is an enzyme that coagulates plasma and blood rather than a toxin that lyses white cells.
Leukocidin
Correct: leukocidin lyses leukocytes, especially neutrophils and macrophages, the cells sent to attack the organism.
Enterotoxin
Enterotoxin induces gastrointestinal distress and causes staphylococcal food intoxication.
Exfoliative toxin
Exfoliative toxin splits the upper layers of the epidermis apart, producing scalded skin syndrome.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: What does toxic shock syndrome toxin induce?
opts: Separation of the epidermis
Splitting the upper layers of the epidermis apart is the work of exfoliative toxin rather than toxic shock syndrome toxin.
Lysis of neutrophils
Lysis of neutrophils and macrophages is the work of leukocidin rather than toxic shock syndrome toxin.
Digestion of blood clots
Digesting blood clots is the enzyme staphylokinase rather than toxic shock syndrome toxin.
Fever, vomiting and shock
Correct: the toxin induces fever, vomiting, shock and systemic organ damage, a toxemia that can end in organ failure.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which staphylococcal lesion is a boil, in which a hair follicle or sebaceous gland progresses into an abscess?
opts: Furuncle
Correct: a furuncle is a boil, inflammation of a hair follicle or sebaceous gland that progresses into an abscess or pustule.
Carbuncle
A carbuncle is the larger, deeper lesion formed when a cluster of furuncles aggregates and interconnects.
Folliculitis
Folliculitis is superficial inflammation of the hair follicle that usually resolves; it can progress to a furuncle.
Impetigo
Impetigo is bubble-like swellings that break and peel away rather than a single follicular abscess.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Where does Staphylococcus capitis live?
opts: Scalp, face and external ear
Correct: Staphylococcus capitis lives on the scalp, face and external ear.
Armpits and groin
The armpits and groin, around the apocrine sweat glands, are the home of Staphylococcus hominis.
Gums and teeth
The gums and teeth are the home of the viridans streptococci.
Vagina and intestine
Skin, intestine and vagina are where Staphylococcus saprophyticus infrequently lives.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Where does Staphylococcus epidermidis normally live?
opts: Skin and mucous membranes
Correct: it lives on skin and mucous membranes, and can cause wound infection by penetrating broken skin.
Scalp, face and external ear
The scalp, face and external ear are the home of Staphylococcus capitis.
Armpit and groin sweat glands
The apocrine sweat glands of the armpits and groin are the home of Staphylococcus hominis.
Human large intestine
The large intestine is where the group D enterococci are normal colonists.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which staphylococcus infrequently lives on skin, intestine and vagina and may cause urinary tract infection?
opts: Staphylococcus hominis
Staphylococcus hominis lives around the apocrine sweat glands of the armpits and groin.
Staphylococcus aureus
Staphylococcus aureus is coagulase positive and is carried mostly in the anterior nares.
Staphylococcus saprophyticus
Correct: Staphylococcus saprophyticus infrequently lives on skin, intestine and vagina and may cause urinary tract infection.
Staphylococcus capitis
Staphylococcus capitis lives on the scalp, face and external ear.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Where does Staphylococcus hominis live?
opts: On the scalp and external ear
The scalp, face and external ear are the home of Staphylococcus capitis.
In the anterior nares
The anterior nares are where humans mostly carry Staphylococcus aureus.
In the vagina and intestine
Skin, intestine and vagina are where Staphylococcus saprophyticus infrequently lives.
Around apocrine sweat glands
Correct: it lives around the apocrine sweat glands of the armpits and groin, which produce sweat with a higher lipid content.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Staphylococcus aureus grows on a selective medium on which streptococci grow poorly. Which property lets it grow there?
opts: It is catalase negative
Staphylococci are catalase POSITIVE; catalase negativity belongs to the streptococci and enterococci.
It needs extra carbon dioxide
Extra carbon dioxide is what Streptococcus pneumoniae and pathogenic Neisseria need, not what lets a staphylococcus grow in salt.
It tolerates high salinity
Correct: Staphylococcus aureus withstands high salinity, so it grows on mannitol salts agar, which is too saline for the streptococci.
It needs blood in the medium
Needing enriched media is the streptococcal trait, and mannitol salts agar is a salt medium rather than a blood one.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: How do streptococci react in the catalase test?
opts: Oxidase positive
Cytochrome oxidase is produced by Neisseria; the streptococcal test result to know is catalase negative.
Catalase negative
Correct: streptococci do not produce catalase, though they do have a peroxidase system; staphylococci are catalase positive.
Catalase positive
Catalase positivity is the staphylococcal result, the bubbling with hydrogen peroxide that separates the two genera.
Coagulase positive
Coagulase positivity identifies Staphylococcus aureus, not a streptococcus.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which of these is alpha hemolytic?
opts: Streptococcus pneumoniae
Correct: Streptococcus pneumoniae and the viridans group are alpha hemolytic, producing partial, greenish hemolysis.
Streptococcus pyogenes
Streptococcus pyogenes is group A and BETA hemolytic, giving complete hemolysis on blood agar.
Streptococcus agalactiae
Streptococcus agalactiae is group B and BETA hemolytic, giving complete rather than partial hemolysis.
Staphylococcus aureus
Staphylococcus aureus produces hemolysins that give beta hemolysis on blood agar.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: A beta-hemolytic streptococcus is bacitracin sensitive. What is it most likely to be?
opts: Streptococcus pyogenes
Correct: bacitracin-sensitive beta-hemolytic streptococci are group A, Streptococcus pyogenes.
Streptococcus agalactiae
Group B streptococci, Streptococcus agalactiae, are bacitracin RESISTANT, as are group C.
Streptococcus pneumoniae
Streptococcus pneumoniae is ALPHA hemolytic and is picked out by optochin sensitivity.
Streptococcus mutans
Streptococcus mutans belongs to the viridans group, which is alpha hemolytic and optochin resistant.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which streptococcus is strictly a human parasite, inhabiting the throat, nasopharynx and occasionally the skin?
opts: Enterococcus faecalis
Enterococcus faecalis colonizes the human and animal intestine rather than being a strictly human throat parasite.
Streptococcus mutans
Streptococcus mutans lives in the oral cavity on the teeth, where its slime layers build plaque.
Streptococcus pyogenes
Correct: group A Streptococcus pyogenes is strictly a human parasite, and humans are its only reservoir.
Streptococcus agalactiae
Streptococcus agalactiae, group B, is found in the cow udder as well as the human vagina, so it is not strictly a human parasite.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: What does M-protein contribute to Streptococcus pyogenes?
opts: Resistance to phagocytosis
Correct: M-protein contributes to its resistance to phagocytosis.
Protection from lysozyme
Protection against lysozyme comes from the C-carbohydrates; M-protein resists phagocytosis instead.
Adherence by short fibers
Short protein fibers for adherence are the fimbriae, a separate surface antigen from the one asked about.
Blocking of complement
Hindering complement and the neutrophil response is the job of C5a protease.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which group A streptococcal sequela causes nephritis and raised blood pressure and can lead to kidney failure?
opts: Urinary tract infection
Urinary tract infection is a direct infection by enterococci or staphylococci, not an immune sequela of group A.
Acute glomerulonephritis
Correct: acute glomerulonephritis causes nephritis and increased blood pressure, and can become chronic, leading to kidney failure.
Rheumatic fever
Rheumatic fever damages the heart valves and causes arthritis, chorea and fever rather than nephritis.
Toxic shock syndrome
Streptococcal toxic shock is a systemic infection, not the kidney sequela that can become chronic.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set1.q: How does group B Streptococcus reach the newborn?
opts: By contaminated food
Food is a route for Streptococcus pyogenes and for staphylococcal enterotoxin rather than for neonatal group B infection.
Through a tooth socket
Dental procedures let viridans streptococci into the blood; group B reaches the newborn during delivery.
During vaginal delivery
Correct: it can be transferred to the infant during vaginal delivery and cause severe infection in the child.
Across the placenta
Group B Streptococcus lives in the mother's vagina and reaches the infant during vaginal delivery; it is not carried across the placenta.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: A pregnant woman is expected to deliver vaginally. What is recommended for group B Streptococcus?
opts: Plan a routine cesarean
Cesarean delivery is not the listed measure; the mother is screened and, if positive, treated during vaginal delivery.
Give lifelong penicillin
Long-term penicillin prophylaxis is for people with a history of rheumatic fever or recurrent strep throat.
Screen her and treat if positive
Correct: pregnant women should be screened and treated, usually with intravenous antibiotics during vaginal delivery.
Vaccinate the infant at birth
No group B vaccine is listed; protection comes from screening the mother and treating during delivery.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which infections do the enterococci cause, particularly in debilitated persons?
opts: Meningitis and septicemia
Meningitis with septicemia is the picture of Neisseria meningitidis, or of group B Streptococcus in newborns.
Pharyngitis and scarlet fever
Pharyngitis and scarlet fever belong to group A Streptococcus pyogenes.
Caries and periodontitis
Dental caries, gingivitis and periodontitis are linked to the viridans streptococci.
Urinary, wound and skin
Correct: enterococci cause opportunistic urinary, wound and skin infections, particularly in debilitated persons.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: A 62-year-old with pre-existing heart valve disease develops endocarditis weeks after a tooth extraction. Which group of organisms is most likely?
opts: Group B streptococci
Group B Streptococcus can cause endocarditis in debilitated patients, but the dental route points to the oral viridans group.
Gram-negative diplococci
Gram-negative diplococci are Neisseria, which are not oral residents entering through a tooth socket.
Viridans streptococci
Correct: a dental procedure lets these oral residents into the blood, and pre-existing heart disease puts the patient at high risk of subacute endocarditis.
Group A streptococci
Group A Streptococcus damages valves through rheumatic fever after pharyngitis rather than by direct infection after dental work.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: What varies among the capsular types of Streptococcus pneumoniae?
opts: Its hemolysis pattern
Streptococcus pneumoniae is alpha hemolytic throughout; what varies is the capsule's specific soluble substance.
Its specific soluble substance
Correct: the specific soluble substance of the capsule varies among types, which is why there are many different capsular types.
Its Lancefield group letter
Streptococcus pneumoniae carries no Lancefield group; its types are capsular.
Its Gram stain reaction
Every type is a Gram-positive coccus; what varies is the specific soluble substance of the capsule.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Pneumococcal infections are usually endogenous. What does that mean?
opts: From another patient's blood
Blood exposure is not the route; endogenous means the infection comes from the host's own flora.
From the person's own flora
Correct: 5 to 50% of people carry it in the nasopharynx, and infection usually comes from that carriage, especially if the host is immunocompromised.
From contaminated surfaces
It is a very delicate bacterium that does not survive long outside its habitat, so surfaces are not the usual source.
From an animal reservoir
No animal reservoir is described; the source is the person's own nasopharyngeal flora.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: What does a candle jar provide when culturing pathogenic Neisseria on chocolate agar?
opts: Extra salt in the medium
Salt selection is the job of mannitol salts agar, which suits staphylococci rather than Neisseria.
Complete absence of air
A candle jar enriches carbon dioxide; Neisseria are aerobic or microaerophilic, not strict anaerobes.
Red cells for hemolysis
Reading hemolysis is the job of blood agar; the candle jar supplies the carbon dioxide.
Enhanced carbon dioxide
Correct: pathogenic species need carbon dioxide-enhanced chambers, such as chocolate agar in a candle jar.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: How is gonococcal conjunctivitis of the newborn prevented?
opts: A conjugate vaccine at birth
The conjugate vaccine is pneumococcal, for children 2 to 23 months; no gonococcal vaccine is listed.
Long-term oral penicillin
Long-term penicillin prophylaxis is for people with a history of rheumatic fever.
Topical antibiotics at birth
Correct: it is prevented by topical antibiotic prophylaxis immediately after birth.
Routine cesarean delivery
Cesarean delivery is not the preventive measure for gonorrhea; topical antibiotic prophylaxis at birth is.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: What is the public health status of gonorrhea?
opts: A vaccine-preventable one
No gonococcal vaccine is listed; vaccines are listed for the meningococcus and pneumococcus.
A reportable disease
Correct: gonorrhea is a reportable infectious disease, and it ranks in the top 5 sexually transmitted diseases.
A zoonotic disease
Gonorrhea is strictly a human infection, so it cannot be zoonotic.
A foodborne disease
Foodborne illness is staphylococcal food intoxication; gonorrhea is sexually transmitted.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set1.q: What gives a presumptive identification of gonorrhea from urethral, vaginal, cervical or eye exudate?
opts: Clusters of cocci in pus
Clusters of Gram-positive cocci point to the staphylococci; the gonococcus is a Gram-negative diplococcus.
Diplococci inside neutrophils
Correct: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci within neutrophils are a presumptive identification.
Lancet pairs in sputum
Lancet-shaped pairs in sputum point to Streptococcus pneumoniae.
Chains of cocci in pus
Chains of Gram-positive cocci point to the streptococci; the gonococcus is a Gram-negative diplococcus.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set1.q: How does Neisseria meningitidis reach the meninges from the nasopharynx?
opts: Through a skin wound
Skin wounds are a portal for staphylococci and streptococci rather than for meningococcal disease.
Through the bloodstream
Correct: disease begins when the bacteria enter the bloodstream, cross the blood-brain barrier, permeate the meninges and grow in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Through the eustachian tube
The eustachian tube carries Streptococcus pneumoniae to the middle ear.
Along peripheral nerves
The route described is the bloodstream, then across the blood-brain barrier.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Which setting raises the risk of meningococcal disease in young adults?
opts: Military field hospitals
Military hospitals are where Acinetobacter baumannii became an important hospital-acquired infection.
Dental surgery suites
Dental procedures let viridans streptococci into the blood; they are not a named risk for this organism.
Tampon use in women
Tampon use is classically associated with staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome.
College dormitories
Correct: carriage is higher in institutional settings, and those living in close quarters, such as college dorms, are at high risk.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set1.q: Where is Branhamella (Moraxella) catarrhalis found in the body?
opts: The large intestine
The large intestine is the home of the enterococci rather than of this Gram-negative coccus.
The apocrine glands
The apocrine sweat glands of the armpits and groin are the home of Staphylococcus hominis.
The heart valves
Heart valves are a site of viridans endocarditis, not a normal habitat.
The nasopharynx
Correct: it is found in the nasopharynx, and the diplococci live on mucous membranes of humans and other primates.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set1.q: A 26-year-old soldier evacuated from Afghanistan develops a multidrug-resistant infection with coccobacilli in a military hospital. Which organism is most likely?
opts: Acinetobacter baumannii
Correct: these multidrug-resistant coccobacilli are becoming an important hospital-acquired infection, especially in military hospitals.
Moraxella catarrhalis
Moraxella catarrhalis is a nasopharyngeal diplococcus, an opportunist in cancer, diabetic and alcoholic patients.
Neisseria meningitidis
Neisseria meningitidis is a diplococcus spread from the nasopharynx in close quarters, not a multidrug-resistant coccobacillus.
Enterococcus faecalis
Enterococcus faecalis is a Gram-positive coccus of the large intestine rather than a Gram-negative coccobacillus.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which feature is true of every staphylococcus?
opts: Coagulase-positive reaction
Only Staphylococcus aureus is coagulase positive; the other staphylococci are grouped as coagulase-negative.
Non-motile and non-spore-forming
Correct: staphylococci lack spores and flagella, so they are always non-spore-forming and non-motile.
Capsule-forming in every strain
Staphylococci MAY produce capsules, a protective layer exterior to the cell wall; it is not true of every one.
Strictly aerobic metabolism
Staphylococcus aureus is a facultative anaerobe that thrives with or without oxygen, so strict aerobic metabolism is wrong.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: What does staphylokinase do?
opts: Inactivates penicillin
Inactivating penicillin is penicillinase, the enzyme behind the resistance of most staphylococci to penicillin.
Digests blood clots
Correct: staphylokinase digests blood clots, the reverse of coagulase, which coagulates plasma and blood.
Coagulates plasma
Coagulating plasma and blood is coagulase, the significant diagnostic trait of Staphylococcus aureus.
Digests connective tissue
Digesting connective tissue is the work of hyaluronidase rather than staphylokinase.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: What is a carbuncle?
opts: An inflamed single follicle
Superficial inflammation of a single hair follicle is folliculitis, which usually resolves without complications.
One boil in a single gland
A boil in one follicle or sebaceous gland that becomes an abscess is a furuncle; a carbuncle is a cluster of them.
Bubble-like peeling blisters
Bubble-like swellings that break and peel away describe impetigo, most common in newborns.
A cluster of joined furuncles
Correct: a carbuncle is a larger, deeper lesion formed by the aggregation and interconnection of a cluster of furuncles.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set2.q: In females, staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome is classically associated with what?
opts: Improper tampon use
Correct: toxic shock syndrome in females classically originates from improper tampon use, a toxemia leading to shock and organ failure.
Contaminated dessert
Food contaminated with heat-stable enterotoxin causes staphylococcal food intoxication rather than toxic shock.
A dental procedure
Dental procedures let viridans streptococci into the blood; they are not the classic source of toxic shock.
Shared bath towels
Shared towels spread staphylococcal skin infection; the classic association of toxic shock in females is tampon use.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which infection may Staphylococcus saprophyticus cause?
opts: Osteomyelitis
Osteomyelitis is a systemic infection of Staphylococcus aureus, established in the metaphysis.
Dental caries
Dental caries is linked to Streptococcus mutans, whose slime layers form the basis of plaque.
Urinary tract infection
Correct: Staphylococcus saprophyticus may cause urinary tract infection.
Scalded skin syndrome
Scalded skin syndrome is a toxigenic disease of Staphylococcus aureus, from exfoliative toxin.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Staphylococcus epidermidis, Staphylococcus hominis and Staphylococcus capitis can all cause which infection?
opts: Wound infection via broken skin
Correct: all three may cause wound infections by penetrating broken skin.
Scalded skin syndrome
Scalded skin syndrome comes from the exfoliative toxin of Staphylococcus aureus.
Food intoxication
Food intoxication comes from the heat-stable enterotoxin of Staphylococcus aureus.
Neonatal meningitis
Neonatal meningitis, pneumonia and sepsis are most often caused by group B Streptococcus.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: After a positive catalase test, which test separates Staphylococcus aureus from the other staphylococci?
opts: Optochin disc
Optochin sensitivity is used among alpha-hemolytic streptococci, to pick out Streptococcus pneumoniae.
Bile esculin test
Bile esculin hydrolysis is a phenotypic culture test listed for the streptococci.
Coagulase test
Correct: Staphylococcus aureus is coagulase positive, while the other staphylococci are coagulase negative.
Bacitracin disc
Bacitracin sensitivity is used among beta-hemolytic streptococci, to pick out group A.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which test distinguishes staphylococci from streptococci and enterococci?
opts: Coagulase test
The coagulase test comes AFTER catalase, separating coagulase-positive Staphylococcus aureus from the other staphylococci.
Bacitracin disc
Bacitracin sensitivity separates group A from other beta-hemolytic streptococci, after the genus is known.
Optochin disc
Optochin sensitivity separates Streptococcus pneumoniae from other alpha-hemolytic streptococci.
Catalase test
Correct: the catalase test with hydrogen peroxide separates catalase-positive staphylococci from catalase-negative streptococci and enterococci.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: A freshly isolated organism is Gram stained as shown. Which genus fits this arrangement?
opts: Streptococcus
Correct: Gram-positive spherical or ovoid cocci arranged in long chains are the streptococci.
Staphylococcus
Staphylococci are Gram-positive cocci in irregular clusters rather than chains.
Neisseria
Neisseria are Gram-negative bean-shaped diplococci rather than purple chains.
Moraxella
Moraxella are Gram-negative diplococci on mucous membranes rather than Gram-positive chains.
set2.alt: Gram-stained smear of a freshly isolated organism, high magnification

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: An alpha-hemolytic streptococcus is optochin sensitive. Which organism is it?
opts: Streptococcus agalactiae
Streptococcus agalactiae is beta hemolytic and bacitracin resistant.
Streptococcus pneumoniae
Correct: among alpha-hemolytic streptococci, optochin sensitivity identifies Streptococcus pneumoniae.
Viridans streptococci
The viridans streptococci are alpha hemolytic but optochin RESISTANT, grouped with the group D streptococci.
Streptococcus pyogenes
Streptococcus pyogenes is BETA hemolytic and identified by bacitracin sensitivity.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: What type of hemolysis surrounds the colonies on this blood agar plate?
opts: Mannitol fermentation
Mannitol fermentation is read on mannitol salts agar by a pH change, not on blood agar.
Complete (beta) hemolysis
Correct: a clear zone around colonies is beta, complete, hemolysis, the reaction of groups A and B.
Partial (alpha) hemolysis
Alpha hemolysis is PARTIAL and greenish rather than the clear zone shown around these colonies.
No hemolysis at all
The clear halos are hemolysis; an unchanged medium around the colonies would be no hemolysis.
set2.alt: Blood agar plate with bacterial colonies

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: What does the change in the medium around and beneath these colonies show?
opts: A positive CAMP test
A positive CAMP test is a flame or arrow shape where the CAMP factor meets Staphylococcus aureus.
Partial (alpha) hemolysis
Correct: alpha, partial, hemolysis gives the greenish color, the reaction of Streptococcus pneumoniae and the viridans group.
Complete (beta) hemolysis
Beta hemolysis is COMPLETE and leaves a clear zone rather than a green one.
Mannitol fermentation
Mannitol fermentation is read by a pH change on mannitol salts agar.
set2.alt: Blood agar plate with bacterial colonies, a second example

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which genus was separated from Streptococcus using 16S ribosomal RNA gene analysis?
opts: Staphylococcus
Staphylococcus is a separate catalase-positive genus that was never part of Streptococcus.
Branhamella
Branhamella was reclassified into Moraxella by 16S analysis; it was never part of Streptococcus.
Enterococcus
Correct: Enterococcus, along with Lactococcus, was separated from Streptococcus in 1984 using 16S ribosomal RNA gene analysis.
Neisseria
Neisseria is a Gram-negative genus that was never part of Streptococcus.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which Streptococcus pyogenes surface antigen contributes most to its resistance to phagocytosis?
opts: M-protein
Correct: M-protein contributes to the resistance of Streptococcus pyogenes to phagocytosis.
C-carbohydrate
The C-carbohydrates protect against lysozyme and are the basis of the Lancefield groups.
Fimbriae
Fimbriae are short protein fibers that give adherence rather than resistance to phagocytosis.
Streptolysin S
Streptolysin S is a hemolysin that causes cell and tissue injury rather than a surface antigen.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set2.q: What is the reservoir of Streptococcus pyogenes?
opts: Farm animals
Animal sources describe some other streptococci, such as groups C and G, which are common animal flora.
Arid soil
Soil is no reservoir of Streptococcus pyogenes; it is strictly a human parasite, and humans are its only reservoir.
Fomites
Fomites can TRANSMIT Streptococcus pyogenes, but the reservoir is humans alone.
Humans only
Correct: it is strictly a human parasite, and humans are the only reservoir; other streptococci may be zoonotic.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which streptococcal skin infection produces lesions like these around the mouth?
opts: Carbuncle
A carbuncle is a deep staphylococcal lesion of interconnected furuncles.
Scarlet fever
Scarlet fever is a systemic infection with fever and a red rash from erythrogenic toxin.
Impetigo
Correct: impetigo (pyoderma) is superficial lesions that break and form a highly contagious crust, often in epidemics in schoolchildren.
Erysipelas
Erysipelas spreads into the dermis and subcutaneous tissues rather than forming superficial crusts.
set2.alt: Close view of skin lesions around a mouth

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which long-term complication of group A streptococcal infection follows pharyngitis and can cause extensive heart valve damage?
opts: Subacute endocarditis
Subacute endocarditis is the most serious viridans infection, from blood-borne bacteria settling on the valves.
Rheumatic fever
Correct: rheumatic fever follows overt or subclinical pharyngitis in children, with carditis, arthritis, chorea and fever.
Glomerulonephritis
Acute glomerulonephritis is the KIDNEY complication: nephritis, raised blood pressure, occasionally heart failure.
Scarlet fever
Scarlet fever is a systemic infection from an erythrogenic-toxin strain, not the valve-damaging sequela itself.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: What is the preventive step against group B streptococcal infection of newborns?
opts: Antibiotic eye ointment
Topical antibiotic prophylaxis at birth prevents GONOCOCCAL conjunctivitis rather than group B infection.
Long-term oral penicillin
Long-term penicillin prophylaxis is for people with a history of rheumatic fever or recurrent strep throat.
Screening and treating mothers
Correct: pregnant women should be screened and treated for group B Streptococcus, with intravenous antibiotics during vaginal delivery.
Vaccinating infants at birth
No group B vaccine is listed; the measure is screening pregnant women and treating those who are positive.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Group B Streptococcus (Streptococcus agalactiae) is the most prevalent cause of which infections?
opts: Pharyngitis in schoolchildren
Pharyngitis in children is the classic disease of group A Streptococcus pyogenes.
Opportunistic urinary infection
Opportunistic urinary infection in debilitated persons is typical of the enterococci.
Neonatal sepsis and meningitis
Correct: it is the most prevalent cause of neonatal pneumonia, sepsis and meningitis.
Dental caries and plaque
Dental caries and plaque are linked to Streptococcus mutans, a viridans streptococcus.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: A beta-hemolytic streptococcus is streaked toward a streak of Staphylococcus aureus. What does the widened zone where the streaks meet show?
opts: A positive CAMP test
Correct: the CAMP factor works synergistically with beta-hemolytic Staphylococcus aureus to give a flame or arrow shape.
Bacitracin sensitivity
Bacitracin sensitivity is read as a zone around the bacitracin disc, and neither disc here shows one.
Partial hemolysis
Partial hemolysis is a greenish zone, not a widened zone where two streaks meet.
A negative CAMP test
A negative CAMP test shows no enhanced zone where the streaks meet.
set2.alt: Blood agar plate with two antibiotic discs on the left and, on the right, a pale streak meeting a perpendicular streak with a widened zone where they meet

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set2.q: How do viridans streptococci usually gain entrance to the body to cause disease?
opts: By invading intact skin
Viridans streptococci are not very invasive on their own; they need a procedure to get in.
Through the birth canal
Passage through the birth canal is how group B Streptococcus and the gonococcus reach newborns.
By aspiration into lungs
Aspiration into the lungs is how Streptococcus pneumoniae causes pneumonia.
Via dental or surgical procedures
Correct: they are not very invasive on their own; dental or surgical procedures may facilitate entrance to the body.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: What is the major virulence factor of Streptococcus pneumoniae?
opts: Its M-protein
M-protein, resisting phagocytosis, is a virulence factor of Streptococcus pyogenes.
Its coagulase
Coagulase is the diagnostic enzyme of Staphylococcus aureus.
Its endotoxin
Endotoxin comes from Gram-negative cells such as Neisseria meningitidis, not from a Gram-positive coccus.
Its large capsule
Correct: all pathogenic strains form large capsules, and the capsule is the major virulence factor.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: How are the pathogenic Neisseria cultured?
opts: Blood agar with optochin
Optochin discs are used to separate alpha-hemolytic streptococci, not to culture Neisseria.
Chocolate agar in a candle jar
Correct: they need enriched complex media and carbon dioxide-enhanced chambers, such as chocolate agar in a candle jar.
Mannitol salts agar in air
Mannitol salts agar selects for salt tolerance, a staphylococcal trait; Neisseria need enriched media and carbon dioxide.
Plain broth in room air
Pathogenic Neisseria need enriched complex media and a carbon dioxide-enhanced chamber.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which gonococcal surface structures aid attachment and slow phagocytosis?
opts: Fimbriae
Correct: fimbriae and other surface molecules give attachment and slow phagocytosis.
Flagella
Neisseria develop no flagella and are non-motile; fimbriae give the gonococcus attachment.
Endospores
Neisseria are non-spore-forming; fimbriae and other surface molecules give attachment and slow phagocytosis.
M-protein
M-protein is the Streptococcus pyogenes antigen that resists phagocytosis.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: A Gram stain of urethral pus is shown. What is the presumptive identification?
opts: Staphylococcus aureus
Staphylococcus aureus would appear as purple, Gram-positive cocci in clusters.
Streptococcus pyogenes
Streptococcus pyogenes would appear as purple, Gram-positive cocci in chains.
Enterococcus faecalis
Enterococci are Gram-positive and catalase negative; Gram-negative pairs in neutrophils point to the gonococcus.
Neisseria gonorrhoeae
Correct: Gram-negative diplococci inside neutrophils in urethral exudate are a presumptive identification of the gonococcus.
set2.alt: Gram stain of urethral pus, high magnification

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Which age groups carry a high risk of meningococcal disease?
opts: 6 months-3 years and 10-20 years
Correct: high-risk groups are children 6 months to 3 years and children and young adults 10 to 20 years, plus anyone living in close quarters.
Newborns and the elderly only
Newborns are at risk from group B Streptococcus, and the elderly from the pneumococcus.
Adults aged 40 to 60 years
Middle-aged adults are not a listed high-risk group; risk peaks in early childhood and at 10 to 20 years.
Children under 2 months only
The early-childhood risk window is 6 months to 3 years, and there is a second at 10 to 20 years.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Where is the human reservoir of Neisseria meningitidis?
opts: The large intestine
The large intestine is the home of the enterococci rather than of this Gram-negative coccus.
The urethra
The urethra is the site of gonococcal infection in males; the meningococcal reservoir is the nasopharynx.
The scalp and ear
The scalp, face and external ear are the home of Staphylococcus capitis.
The nasopharynx
Correct: the human reservoir is the nasopharynx, in 3 to 30% of the adult population, and higher in institutional settings.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Who may need prophylactic treatment when a patient has meningococcal disease?
opts: No one at all
Prophylaxis of family members and children in close contact may be indicated, and of medical personnel after direct exposure to secretions.
Only the patient
The patient is TREATED; close contacts may need prophylaxis.
Close contacts
Correct: prophylaxis of family members and children in close contact may be indicated, and of medical personnel only after direct exposure to the patient's secretions.
The whole city
Prophylaxis is aimed at close contacts, such as family and children nearby, rather than a whole city, and medical personnel only after direct exposure.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, and methods of treatment, and prevention of cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Into which genus has Branhamella catarrhalis been reclassified?
opts: Enterococcus
Enterococcus is a Gram-positive genus split from Streptococcus.
Moraxella
Correct: 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequence analyses moved it into the closely related genus Moraxella.
Neisseria
Neisseria is a separate genus of the family, home of the gonococcus and the meningococcus.
Acinetobacter
Acinetobacter is a separate genus of multidrug-resistant coccobacilli, not the new home of Branhamella.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire cocci of medical importance
set2.q: Where has Acinetobacter baumannii become an important hospital-acquired infection?
opts: Military hospitals
Correct: it is becoming an important hospital-acquired infection, especially in military hospitals.
Dental clinics
Dental procedures are the route for viridans streptococci; Acinetobacter is a problem in military hospitals.
College dormitories
Dormitories are a high-risk setting for Neisseria meningitidis.
Newborn nurseries
Newborns are at risk from group B Streptococcus and gonococcal conjunctivitis acquired at birth.
